messages.subject: Vectorizing question
parts:
Hi,

While looking through math functions only in C++11 cmath, I noticed that asinh, acosh, and atanh are only available in C++11. So, to vectorize them, I switched to using the boost version of these functions. While asinh passes the tests, acosh and atanh don't because the boost version handles invalid input differently than the rev and fwd versions.  

Here's some of the rev mode code for atan (acosh and asinh are similar): 

class atanh_vari : public op_v_vari {

      public:

        atanh_vari(double val, vari* avi) :

          op_v_vari(val, avi) {

        }

        void chain() {

          avi_->adj_ += adj_ / (1.0 - avi_->val_ * avi_->val_);

        }

      };


and some of the fwd mode code for atanh (acosh and asinh are similar):


template <typename T>

    inline fvar<T> atanh(const fvar<T>& x) {

      using ::atanh;

      using stan::math::square;

      return fvar<T>(atanh(x.val_), x.d_ / (1 - square(x.val_)));

    }


Shouldn't they use the boost version throughout all modes? If so, should I create an issue for this?


Best,

Rayleigh

You can write a stan::math version that imports Boost and
handles invalid input consistently.

We haven't been super consistent on handling invalid input
because I was trying to have our autodiff library have the
same invalid input handling as the std lib (that is, log
returns NaN rather than throwing an exception if you
give it a negative input).

Yes, they should ideally be using the same implementation.
And they should have behavior consistent with the std:: library,
at least for now and at least where possible.

It's a huge pain, but you have to learn how to debug yourself.
It took Daniel and I a long time for C++ and you can see we're
still spending a huge amount of time trying to help you on this
one issue (though it's really a bunch of little issues).

The design's another issue, like what our error behavior should
be --- please do keep bringing these issues up.

- Bob
